records.title: The suspected ignition mechanism
records.supports: An electrical arc was the most probable initiating mechanism identified by the Board.
records.limit: The precise initiating arc, wire, and location were not conclusively proved.
records.rights: Text linked as source; no illustrations reproduced.

records.title: Crew training is context, not telemetry
records.supports: NASA catalogs S66-58038 as a 1966 preflight crew-training photograph.
records.limit: A crew-training photograph does not record the January 1967 cabin fire or prove oxygen pressure.
records.rights: NASA photo catalog linked; image reproduction not included or approved for product promotion.

records.title: Damage was photographed afterward
records.supports: NASA catalogs S67-21294 as the command-module interior after the fire.
records.limit: Visible damage is not a contemporaneous ignition recording and cannot identify the first spark.
records.rights: NASA photo catalog linked; no image downloaded or reproduced.

records.title: A memorial display, fifty years later
records.supports: NASA announced a 2017 exhibit that included a historic Apollo 1 hatch.
records.limit: The 2017 display records how the accident was presented later, not how ignition occurred in 1967.
records.rights: Source link only; museum imagery and any depicted likeness require separate item review for commerce.

records.title: Later fire tests were deliberate
records.source_name: NASA: 50 Years Ago — Apollo Flammability Tests
records.supports: NASA described 102 deliberately initiated Command Module fires in its retrospective on 1967–68 testing.
records.limit: The retrospective publication date is not the test date; reproduced fire dynamics do not prove the accident’s precise spark.
records.rights: Source link only; any third-party embedded media require separate review.
